content:
chen.cs: Customer on Dedicated pool `redwood-ded-42` reporting sudden throughput drop and a lot of 429s since ~10:05 UTC. They see tail latency 500-2k ms and tokens/sec down ~4x. Can we triage?
priya.support: Thanks — raised a support ticket, customer sent request_ids: r-9a3f, r-9a50. They say this started immediately after today's autoscaler policy change.
jamie.eng: I pulled the metrics. cluster tokens/sec on that pool dropped from ~120k to ~30k at 10:06. Continuous-batcher avg_batch_size collapsed from ~48 -> ~6.
jamie.eng: quick observables:
```
metric: continuous_batcher.avg_batch_size 48 -> 6
metric: scheduler.pending_queues 18 -> 72
metric: per_tenant_small_req_ratio 0.12 -> 0.67
logs: lots of "assembled batch size=3, wait_ms=2" entries
```
priya.support: Customer also attached a sample workload: many tiny prompts (~20 tokens) across 40 concurrent clients.
margo.sre: That screams batch fragmentation + fair-queue per-tenant throttling. If lots of tiny requests from many tenants, scheduler creates many small microbatches and we lose GPU efficiency.
riley.infra: Autoscaler: no new nodes were added after the policy tweak; there was a bug to ignore scale-up when average_batch_size < 10 — that would prevent us from adding capacity when microbatches dominate.
jamie.eng: Repro steps I used:
1) k8s exec into runner: `kubectl exec -n runtime runner-0 -- /bin/sh`
2) run synthetic load: `python loadgen.py --concurrency 40 --prompt_size 20 --qps 400 --tenant-mix 1`
3) tail logs: `tail -n 200 /var/log/runner/continuous_batcher.log | grep assembled`
Observed same tiny batches.
chen.cs: Customer asked for a mitigation ASAP — they can't tolerate the 4x throughput hit.
jamie.eng: Short-term mitigations:
- Manual scale-up: bump dedicated pool by +4 GPUs to reduce queueing pressure (riley+infra).
- Temporarily relax autoscaler guard: allow scale-ups even when avg_batch_size < 10 (ops).
- Enable request aggregation for that tenant: turn on `bundler.compact_mode=true` for cluster as a stopgap.
I can run the bundler flip as a config flag with low risk.
riley.infra: I'll do manual scale up now and monitor. running: `infractl scale pool redwood-ded-42 --add 4`
ops-bot: deploy request received: infractl scaling command queued (req 8672).
margo.sre: Medium-term: we should tune scheduler to avoid headway oscillation and allow small-wait batching. Proposed changes:
- increase `max_batch_tokens` from 2048 -> 8192 to allow batching more small requests into one pass.
- increase `wait_ms` default from 2 -> 8 for dedicated pools with high small-req ratio.
- remove autoscaler dependency on avg_batch_size threshold; instead rely on queue_depth and latency windows.
jamie.eng: Also found config from yesterday: `scheduler.fair_queue_per_tenant=true` with weights normalized but no weight_floor. Many tenants got equal weight and starved big throughput tenants. Suggest add `weight_floor=0.05` to keep minimal fairness.
priya.support: I communicated the temporary actions to customer (manual scale + bundler toggle). They said they can roll with temporary scaling but want a postmortem + guardrails.
chen.cs: customer asked for exact commands so they can correlate request ids — gave them the logs and the `continuous_batcher` entries.
jamie.eng: I kicked the bundler flip for that pool: `runtimectl set --pool redwood-ded-42 bundler.compact_mode true` — will monitor. Watch metrics: continuous_batcher.avg_batch_size and gpu_util.
ops-bot: config change applied to pool redwood-ded-42, change_id c-4421.
jamie.eng: Early signals: avg_batch_size rising from 6 -> 22, gpu_util up ~30%. tail latency improving.
margo.sre: Action items:
- jamie to open a perf PR that changes defaults for wait_ms and max_batch_tokens (canary first).
- riley to add autoscaler fix to ignore avg_batch_size guard for 30d hotfix.
- priya to draft customer postmortem and timeline.
- chen to collect request_ids for full trace and attach to incident.
priya.support: I'll coordinate with customer on verification and timeline for rollback of bundler once stable.
riley.infra: Scale job finished, nodes ready.
jamie.eng: Will run canary with updated scheduler params on a single node later today. If canary passes, roll to pool and push runbook changes.
chen.cs: Thanks team. Customer pinged: throughput back to ~85% of normal after scale + bundler. They said they saw far fewer 429s.
priya.support: Marking this thread as active incident. I'll link ticket #INC-2026-114 and follow up on postmortem. :thumbsup:
margo.sre: We should also add a monitoring alert: when avg_batch_size drops below 12 AND tokens/sec drops >30% -> fire a regression alert to eng-runtime channel.
jamie.eng: Agreed. I'll add alert rule and a short remediation section in runbook.
chen.cs: closing loop with customer now, will update once they validate production traffic for 4 hours.
priya.support: moving to follow-up, thanks all :heart:
